::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How to read this report"}

These definitions assume familiarity with frequentist statistics but no prior Bayesian training. `METHODS.md` provides the full glossary.

- **Posterior distribution.** The distribution of a quantity after combining the priors and data under the model. Reports summarise it with a median and intervals.
- **Credible interval.** Given the model and data, an 89% credible interval contains the quantity with 89% probability. Reports show inner 50% and outer 89% equal-tailed intervals alongside the full posterior. These coverages are reporting conventions, not decision thresholds or guarantees of simulation precision.
- **Prediction interval.** A credible interval describes uncertainty about a model quantity, such as a mean effect. A prediction interval describes uncertainty about a future score, including variation between observations. The findings box uses credible intervals.
- **ROPE and δ.** The region of practical equivalence runs from −δ to +δ and represents effects judged too small to matter. The education lead chose the initial minimally important difference δ after inspecting results. ITT reports therefore show sensitivity to other δ values; see `METHODS.md` for the standing rule for later outcomes.
- **Causal and association labels.** Randomisation balances baseline characteristics in expectation, not exactly in this sample. Causal interpretations also require the stated available-case and model assumptions. Skill and dose coefficients remain adjusted associations that can reflect confounding.
- **Logits and items.** The logit is the log-odds scale used to model bounded scores. Headlines translate effects into test items or, for floor outcomes, percentage points.
- **Beta-Binomial.** This working likelihood models a count out of a fixed maximum and allows more variation than a Binomial with the same mean. Predictive checks assess whether it describes the observed score distribution.
- **Convergence and release.** Check R-hat, effective sample size, divergences and sampling energy before interpretation. A failed computation gate withholds findings. Passing it does not establish model fit or causal identification; release also requires the other checks stated in the report.

:::
